definitions.explanation: The act of accepting, receiving, or admitting someone or something. Used for people (refugees, patients, students) as well as abstract concepts (proposals, conditions).

examples.japanese: {難民|なんみん}の{受|う}け{入|い}れ。
{留学生|りゅうがくせい}の{受|う}け{入|い}れ{体制|たいせい}を{整|ととの}える。
examples.english: To prepare a system for accepting international students.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}{住民|じゅうみん}の{受|う}け{入|い}れなしには、この{計画|けいかく}は{進|すす}められない。
examples.english: This plan cannot proceed without acceptance from local residents.

notes:
The nominal form of the verb {受|う}け{入|い}れる (to accept). Very commonly used as a noun modifier in compound expressions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {受|う}け{入|い}れ{態勢|たいせい}: acceptance system/setup
- {受|う}け{入|い}れ{先|さき}: receiving party; host institution
- {受|う}け{入|い}れ{可能|かのう}: acceptable; able to be accepted
- {患者|かんじゃ}の{受|う}け{入|い}れ: admission of patients
- {条件|じょうけん}の{受|う}け{入|い}れ: acceptance of conditions

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {受容|じゅよう}: acceptance — more abstract and literary; used in psychology and academic contexts
- {承認|しょうにん}: approval — implies formal authorization, not just acceptance
- {容認|ようにん}: tolerance; tacit approval — accepting something reluctantly or without opposing it

REGISTER:
Neutral to slightly formal. Very common in news, policy discussions, and institutional contexts.
